Voznesensk New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Voznesensk, Ukraine

Demolished. This cemetery's history is unclear, presumably existing by the early 20th century; the IAJGS database references an untraced 1918 gravestone, though the older section does hold confirmed prewar tombstones, including one from 1937 - though these may have been relocated from Voznesensk's Old cemetery, destroyed during WWII. The local community cares for the site today; vandals moved ten tombstones from their original places about six months before this survey, since restored. Jews likely began settling in Voznesensk after the Russo-Turkish Wars, from the late 18th to early 19th century; population reached 778 by 1863, the same year a synagogue opened. Population reached 5,932 (38%) by 1897; by 1909, two government boys'/girls' schools and a Talmud Torah operated, with seven synagogues by 1910. In 1925, seven Voznesensk Jewish families founded a Jewish farming society in the Kherson region. Population peaked at 6,177 by 1920, falling to 2,843 by 1939. Nazi occupation from August 6, 1941 saw 3,174 regional residents executed, most of them Jewish. A Jewish population persisted after WWII; today the community numbers 48 people.
